title: Bacteria in a root nodule
hook: Compare the effects on both participants.

knows: Ecological interactions can affect participants differently.
doesNotKnow: Both partners benefit in the specified association, an example of mutualism. The details of nitrogen transfer are simplified.

misconception: An interaction must affect both participants in the same way.
objective: Classify the stated effects of an ecological interaction.

claims.text: Question, diagram and reveal: In this root-nodule association, bacteria obtain plant resources and provide fixed nitrogen to the legume. Using + for benefit, − for harm and 0 for no appreciable effect, which signs describe Rhizobia and Legume, in that order? Rhizobia: +; Legume: +. Both partners benefit in the specified association, an example of mutualism. The details of nitrogen transfer are simplified.
claims.source: Stipulated simplified example; ecological definitions: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-6-community-ecology

claims.text: Icons and signs summarize the stipulated interaction and do not quantify fitness or capture every ecological effect.
